line: All these guns in the car, I gotta wear a seatbelt I ain’t got no license, so I gotta wear my seatbelt (Skrrt)
vault_lines: Live by the code, die by the code, never been a ho
meaning:
21 has boasted about driving without a license before, first on his July 2017 track, “Bad Business,” and second on Gucci Mane’s December 2018 track, “Just Like It”:


I ain’t got no license, but I still drive, dawg (Yeah)

Savage still ride with no license (21, facts)


21 was born in the London Borough of Newham and at the age of seven, he moved to Atlanta. In a February 2019 New York Times interview, he commented on when he first fully realized he was not an American citizen:

Probably like the age when you start to get your driver’s license. I couldn’t never take driver’s ed, I couldn’t never go get a job. About that age.

On February 3, 2019, 21 was arrested by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for overstaying his visa, but he also allegedly had a gun in his possession at the time of the arrest.

Coincidentally, in early November 2019, 21 was allowed to get a driver’s license and appear on TV.

line: Feel like Mozzy, I got one up top (Yeah)

Mozzy, a rapper hailing from Sacramento, California, is known for using the term “1 Up Top” in his music, most notably his August 2017 album, 1 Up Top Ahk. Earlier, in November 2016, Mozzy also dropped a preparatory EP called 1 Up Top Finna Drop.

As of this song’s release, Mozzy and Savage haven’t worked together musically. Mozzy appears earlier on this album on the track, “Carmen Electra.”
